title: The Last Time Through the Door

lines.text: I remember the first time I turned the key
Empty rooms and a quieter me
I remember the first time I turned the key
Empty rooms and a quieter me
Didn’t know what these walls would hold
Just a new beginning, clean and cold
Every laugh and every fight
Every late-night talk and morning light
Built a life I didn’t see
Until I had to leave
Now I’m walking through the door one last time
Same old frame, different eyes
All the years still linger here
In the dust and the air
I never thought the first step in
Would hurt this much walking out again
Boxes stacked where the couch used to be
Echoes left of who I used to be
I trace the marks we made on the floor
Knowing I won’t open this door anymore
Every laugh and every fight
Every late-night talk and morning light
Built a life I didn’t see
Until I had to leave
Now I’m walking through the door one last time
Same old frame, different eyes
All the years still linger here
In the dust and the air
I never thought the first step in
Would hurt this much walking out again
It’s strange how a doorway can hold so much
A thousand small moments in a single touch
I pause with my hand on the frame
Whisper goodbye to a place that became
Now I’m walking through the door one last time
Same old frame, different eyes
All the years still linger here
In the dust and the air
I never thought the first step in
Would hurt this much walking out again
